cf.title: Fix races in Windows pthread emulation

input.subject: [PATCH v1] Fix races in Windows pthread emulation

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal or the compare-and-exchange fix. Several people reproduced the hang, and the cost falls only on Windows builds of libpq and ECPG. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-1, is a fixable design point: v2 adds a per-compiler atomic load to two copies of the mutex code, and Heikki Linnakangas asked for one primitive in message #8. A committer who knows the Windows port must decide that point and the backpatch range.

brief.title: Fix race in Windows pthread mutex initialization emulation
brief.problem: The Windows pthread mutex emulation in ECPG and libpq lets a waiting thread overwrite the initialized state 1 with state 2. pthread_mutex_unlock then returns EINVAL and leaves the critical section locked, so threaded client code hangs. The ECPG thread/alloc test hangs on native ARM64 and on the AMD64 buildfarm animal hamerkop.
brief.proposed_design: Only the thread that changes initstate from 0 with a compare-and-exchange initializes the critical section and publishes state 1. The lock fast path uses an acquire load, and unlock uses a relaxed load after a successful lock. v2 drops the v1 change of pthread_once_t from bool to LONG and leaves type layouts unchanged.
author_claims: The existing ECPG thread/alloc test exercises the failing path and reproduced the hang, so no new test is added.
A deterministic reproducer returns EINVAL on the old code and passes with v2.
Stress tests passed 800,000 lock/unlock pairs per configuration on native ARM64 MSVC, emulated x64 MSVC and emulated x64 MinGW.
v2 applies cleanly to REL_17_STABLE and REL_18_STABLE, but neither branch was built.
The fast-path cost is not benchmarked, and the change touches no non-Windows code or user-facing interface.
brief.thread_state: Heikki Linnakangas accepted the v2 approach but asked whether one atomic load works for both MSVC and MinGW instead of ReadAcquire and __atomic_load_n. Alexander Lakhin reported that v2 removes the hang in 600 stress iterations, and backpatching plus the separate pthread_once fix stay open.
unclear: The material does not say whether the fix should be backpatched, or to which branches.
The pthread_once ordering issue on ARM64 is dropped from v2, and no follow-up patch is posted.
The material does not say whether the second CommitFest entry 7255 is a duplicate of 7131.
The material does not say how v2 interacts with CommitFest entry 6314, which moves libpq pthread code into src/port.
The commit message for v2 is not shown; only the v1 commit message is visible.

objections.title: Ad hoc compiler-specific atomic loads added to two duplicated copies
objections.failure_scenario: A later fix or a new Windows toolchain changes the ordering code in the libpq copy but not in the ECPG copy, or only in the MSVC branch. The MinGW branch has less coverage on the buildfarm. The drift shows up months later as a rare hang in client threads.
objections.argument: v2 adds an `#ifdef _MSC_VER` split, with ReadAcquire on MSVC and __atomic_load_n on other compilers, to two copies of the same mutex code. Heikki asked for one primitive for both compilers in message #8, and message #9 leaves that open. Postgres already has its own atomics and barrier abstraction, and the proposal does not say why that is unusable here. CF entry 6314 would merge the libpq copy into src/port (message #1), so the order of the two patches decides how many copies need this code.
objections.author_must_show: Why can the fast path not use the existing Postgres atomics or barrier primitives, or one shared helper, instead of a per-compiler branch in each copy?

critic.reasoning: Heikki asked for one primitive in message #8, and message #9 leaves the per-compiler split open without a benchmark. The two copies predate the patch and port/atomics.h rejects frontend code, so neither point should count as support.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch touches the ECPG header ecpg-pthread-win32.h; v2 says it keeps type layouts unchanged, after v1 changed pthread_once_t.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The bug is in released client libraries; v2 applies to REL_17_STABLE and REL_18_STABLE but neither branch was built.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: v2 adds an MSVC and non-MSVC atomic load branch to two copies of the mutex code, in ECPG and libpq.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The lock and unlock fast paths of the Windows client mutex gain an atomic load, and the cost is not benchmarked.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Why can the lock fast path not use one atomic load primitive, or one shared helper, for both MSVC and MinGW in both copies?
Which back branches should get this fix, and do REL_17_STABLE and REL_18_STABLE build and pass the ECPG and libpq tests with v2?
Should this patch or CommitFest entry 6314 go in first, given that 6314 moves the libpq copy into src/port?
Is the pthread_once ordering problem on ARM64 still real after v2, and will a separate patch for it follow?
Is CommitFest entry 7255 a duplicate of 7131, and which one should be closed?

committability.owner_note: Heikki Linnakangas reviewed v2 in the thread and accepted the approach. The owner needs to know the Windows port and the thread-safety code of libpq and ECPG.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the correctness of a lock-free init state machine in two client libraries on MSVC and MinGW, on x64 and ARM64, in every branch that gets the fix. Races of this kind show up rarely and late, and MinGW has less buildfarm coverage.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 after review and dropped the pthread_once change that was questioned. No follow-up patch for pthread_once is posted.

priority.reason: The patch fixes a reproduced hang for threaded Windows clients of libpq and ECPG, and it also removes a test hang seen in CI and on the buildfarm animal hamerkop. It is about 4 KiB in three client-side files, adds no user-visible surface, and has one open point about the atomic load primitive.

provisional_note: The code and the v2 commit message were not read, so the memory ordering of the new loads on ARM64 and the layout claim for ecpg-pthread-win32.h are unchecked. Messages #4 to #10 are known only from the brief and the reviewer notes.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use internal pthreads reimplementation only when building with MSVC
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the guards around libpq's and ecpg's internal minimal pthreads reimplementation from WIN32 to _MSC_VER, so MinGW builds use winpthreads. The author, who builds mingw-postgresql on Fedora, reported that on MinGW the internal implementation causes symbol collisions with winpthreads.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Alvaro Herrera asked whether build-system changes were needed to use winpthreads and why the existing MinGW buildfarm members build correctly without the change. He also suggested a buildfarm animal for the Fedora MinGW build. The author did not answer, so after the entry sat in Waiting on Author, Daniel Gustafsson returned it with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If none are needed, why are all our mingw buildfarm members building
correctly?

precedents_retrieved.title: Make ECPG locale usage thread-safe
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread started as a proposal to drop the HAVE_USELOCALE configure check and require uselocale(3) on all non-Windows platforms. The remaining patch in CF entry #5166 changes the ECPG library to use thread-safe locale functions with a shared C locale_t, so it no longer switches the global locale.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed the ECPG patch, then reverted it the same day after buildfarm members such as jackdaw failed to link test_json_parser_incremental_shlib with an undefined pthread_once from libpgport_shlib.a. Masahiko Sawada saw the failure only with make, not meson, and Álvaro Herrera suspected a missing -pthread in the test_json_parser build. No one picked the patch up again, and Peter said it would have to be committed again and debugged on the buildfarm, so the stale entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Yeah, looks like we'll have to revert this for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid use deprecated Windows Memory API
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Alvaro Herrera, Daniel Gustafsson, Michael Paquier
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch replaces LocalAlloc/LocalFree calls in Postgres Windows code with HeapAlloc/HeapFree on the default process heap. The author cited Microsoft documentation that recommends the heap functions for new applications.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers found no benefit: the code is not performance-sensitive, LocalAlloc is not deprecated, and Microsoft's own documentation calls the choice a matter of personal preference. Alvaro Herrera judged the patch useless and the new code less clean, and Michael Paquier recommended rejection, citing Daniel's and Alvaro's arguments.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I was looking at this thread, and echoing Daniel's and Alvaro's
arguments, I don't quite see why this patch is something we need.

precedents_retrieved.title: meson: Adjust test timeout for Valgrind builds
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes meson detect Valgrind builds with a compiler check for USE_VALGRIND and raise the per-test timeout from 1000s to 10000s in that case. It handles USE_VALGRIND passed through -Dc_args, CPPFLAGS or CFLAGS, and autoconf needs no change because it sets no test timeout.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund replied that the usual way to handle slow Valgrind runs is to pass --timeout-multiplier to meson test, so no build change is needed. The author answered that a default would be more user friendly, but nobody replied after that and the entry was withdrawn. The visible messages do not show the reason for the withdrawal.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The usual way to deal with that is to pass --timeout-multiplier=100 or
something like that to meson test.

precedents_retrieved.title: Safer hash table initialization macro
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a macro, HASH_ELEM_INIT, that sets keysize and entrysize from a named key member and checks at compile time that the key is the first member of the entry struct. The thread grew into a larger patch series by Jelte Fennema-Nio with new hash table creation functions (hash_make and variants), automatic string or blob key detection, and a foreach_hash iteration macro.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last visible messages are positive reviews and fixes from late January 2026, and no message shows the withdrawal or a deciding objection.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove redundant initializations
precedents_retrieved.summary: Peter Eisentraut proposed removing code that sets each struct field to zero right after makeNode() or memset() has already zeroed the whole struct. He kept initializations that carry nontrivial comments or keep symmetry between branches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback after waiting on author for three weeks: the patch no longer applied on HEAD, and no rebased version was posted. Before that, Tom Lane objected that explicit initialization of every field is an intended style, which helps when adding a new field and avoids depending on all-zero-bits values. Noah Misch later supported the idea and offered to review it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This has been sitting in the CF app for three weeks waiting on author,
so I have marked this entry as RwF for now:

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix error message for statement_timeout and fix flaky test
precedents_retrieved.summary: The entry proposed a fix to the statement timeout logic, where a query that hit statement_timeout could report "canceling statement due to user request" instead of a timeout error. It also changed the flaky postgres_fdw cancel test by moving it before use_remote_estimate is enabled and raising its statement_timeout from 10ms to 100ms.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last message, from the author on the day of the decision, posts the test fix and says the test should be removed if failures continue. No objection to either patch appears.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix TOCTOU race in ReplicationSlotsComputeRequiredLSN()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moved LWLockRelease(ReplicationSlotControlLock) in ReplicationSlotsComputeRequiredLSN() to after the call to XLogSetReplicationSlotMinimumLSN(), so a stale minimum LSN cannot overwrite a lower one. It copied the fix that commit 2a5225b99d7 made for ReplicationSlotsComputeRequiredXmin() and was proposed for backpatching.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch widened the lock scope only on the read side and left the lock level in ReplicationSlotReserveWal() unchanged, so it did not fix the race. Another commitfest entry already addressed the same issue, and the author withdrew this one.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The patch you posted
only increases the lock scope in ReplicationSlotsComputeRequiredLSN() but does
not increase the lock level when reserving WALs, so I think it would not
fix the issue.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 728f86fec65537eade8d9e751961782ddb527934.

The signal handling was a few bricks shy of a load in that commit,
which made the walreceiver non-responsive to SIGTERM while it was
waiting for the connection to be established. That prevented a standby
from being promoted.

Since it was non-essential refactoring, let's revert it to make v16
work the same as earlier releases. I reverted it in 'master' too, to
keep the branches in sync. The refactoring was a good idea as such,
but it needs a bit more work. Once we have developed a complete patch
with this issue fixed, let's re-apply that to 'master'.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE"".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE"".
Reverted commit(s): Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE".
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 98fc31d6499163a0a781aa6f13582a07f09cd7c6.
That change allowed DROP OWNED BY to drop grants of the target
role to other roles, arguing that nobody would need those
privileges anymore.  But that's not so: if you're not superuser,
you still need admin privilege on the target role so you can
drop it.

It's not clear whether or how the dependency-based approach
to solving the original problem can be adapted to keep these
grants.  Since v18 release is fast approaching, the sanest
thing to do seems to be to revert this patch for now.  The
race-condition problem is low severity and not worth taking
risks for.

I didn't force a catversion bump in 98fc31d64, so I won't do
so here either.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no earlier attempt at the same or a similar idea, and the thread mentions no earlier discussion of this race. The thread refers only to CommitFest entry 6314, a pending refactor that moves the libpq code into src/port without changing this state machine (message #1), and to entry 7255, created by a reviewer to track this same patch (message #3). Neither is a prior rejection, so this angle has nothing to object to.

Nothing in the user-facing contract changes: no SQL, GUC, psql, pg_dump or driver-visible behaviour, and v2 keeps the existing type layouts, including in ecpg-pthread-win32.h. Backpatch target branches are still open, and REL_17_STABLE and REL_18_STABLE were not built (message #7), but that is a testing step and does not change the design.

v2 has no persistent or cross-node state. It changes only the in-process Windows mutex emulation in libpq and ECPG, with no on-disk, WAL, catalog or protocol change. Message #7 says v2 keeps the existing type layouts, which drops the v1 pthread_once_t change that message #4 questioned for backpatching. Without the code, I could not check whether the installed ecpg-pthread-win32.h exposes anything that the new atomic loads would affect for applications built against older headers.

The patch fixes a client-side race in the Windows pthread mutex emulation in ECPG and libpq. It adds no privilege, role, setting, data path or interface that an unprivileged user could use, and it changes no server-side behaviour. A hang in a threaded client is a bug in the client's own process, so it does not give a denial-of-service path against other users.
The fix targets a real hang that several people reproduced, and its cost falls only on Windows client builds. The objection above is about how the code is placed, not whether to fix the bug.

This is a fix for a real hang that two independent reporters and the buildfarm reproduced, and no existing feature or extension removes the need for it. A committer might suggest native Windows primitives such as SRWLOCK or InitOnceExecuteOnce instead of the custom init state, but that is a design choice for a possibly backpatched bugfix and does not argue against the fix.

This is a bug fix for a hang in shipped client libraries, so demand is shown. Independent reports: Nazir Bilal Yavuz hit it twice in CI (messages #2, #3), the buildfarm animal hamerkop failed twice this year (message #5), and Alexander Lakhin reproduced it on x86_64 (messages #5, #10). The cost falls only on Windows builds of ECPG and libpq, and no user-facing surface changes.
